source: Hurry hurry has no blessing
note: Said to anyone rushing a job. It is also why this app is called PolePole.

source: Little by little fills the measure
note: A kibaba is a small grain measure. The Swahili case for showing up daily.

source: Slowly slowly is indeed the way
note: Pole pole is the pace you hear most often in Tanzania — for walking, working and learning.

source: Where there is a will, there is a way
note: Almost word for word the English proverb: nia is will, njia is path.

source: Patience attracts blessings
note: Often shortened to just subira when someone is losing their temper.

source: The patient one eats the ripe fruit
note: Wait, and you get the good mango rather than the green one.

source: If you do not seal the crack, you will build a wall
note: Deal with the small problem now or rebuild the whole thing later.

source: One finger cannot kill a louse
note: You need both thumbs — so, you need other people.

target: Akili ni nywele, kila mtu ana zake
source: Intelligence is like hair, everyone has their own
note: A gracious way to disagree with someone.

source: One who wants what is under the bed must bend down
note: Mvungu is the space beneath a bed. Nothing worth having comes without stooping for it.

source: A stick that is far away will not kill a snake
note: Help that is not here is not help.

source: Let the guest come so the host may benefit
note: Hospitality as an exchange, not a favour — the heart of Swahili karibu.

source: The hasty one never gets to eat the sweet thing
note: Pupa is greedy haste. The impatient leave before dessert.

target: Asiyefunzwa na mamaye hufunzwa na ulimwengu
source: One not taught by their mother will be taught by the world
note: The world is a harsher teacher, and it charges more.

target: Maji ukiyavulia nguo huna budi kuyaoga
source: Once you have undressed for the water, you must bathe
note: The Swahili answer to in for a penny, in for a pound.

source: After hardship comes relief
note: Said to someone going through something difficult.

target: Haraka haraka ina baraka ya punda
source: Great haste carries only a donkey's blessing
note: A wry extension of the first proverb, for when someone ignores it.

source: The sign of rain is clouds
note: Every big thing announces itself first, if you are watching.

source: The one who endures eats what is ripe
note: A close cousin of mvumilivu hula mbivu — endurance rather than patience.

source: If you want what is in the corner, you must bend
note: A common variant you will hear alongside the mvunguni version.
